### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **4** package(s): `@objectstack/downstream-contract`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, `@objectstack/types`, touching **48** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/integration.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/integration.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/integration.json`, …), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**24** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3a2f4c008d5897137c5e1f4e9ceec85f630d9aa7`.

⛔ **6** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **8** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/spec/api-surface/integration.json`, `packages/spec/authorable-surface/integration.json`, `packages/spec/declaration-map/integration.json`, …) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **12** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **58** of **210** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **170** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3a2f4c008d5897137c5e1f4e9ceec85f630d9aa7` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `ebbe79274c5666500079a04572823ac7e62a984d` — the merge of head `c9b16a83881491e0566788582025c012aefad06a` into base `3a2f4c008d5897137c5e1f4e9ceec85f630d9aa7`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin ebbe79274c5666500079a04572823ac7e62a984d && git checkout ebbe79274c5666500079a04572823ac7e62a984d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 3a2f4c008d5897137c5e1f4e9ceec85f630d9aa7 c9b16a83881491e0566788582025c012aefad06a && git checkout -B drift-repro 3a2f4c008d5897137c5e1f4e9ceec85f630d9aa7 && git merge --no-ff c9b16a83881491e0566788582025c012aefad06a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 3a2f4c008d5897137c5e1f4e9ceec85f630d9aa7
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 3a2f4c008d5897137c5e1f4e9ceec85f630d9aa7` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `c9b16a83881491e0566788582025c012aefad06a`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider.ts, packages/spec/src/integration/connector.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.connector-auth-config-oauth2-retired.ts, packages/spec/src/migrations/registry.ts.template, packages/spec/src/shared/connector-auth.zod.ts + docs/adr/0143-outbound-connector-auth-is-open-tier.md (read on `main`, the ruling the schema implements), packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts and src/connector-credential-source.ts (the first consumers of the widened union, seat ruling A), packages/types/src/connector-credential-source.ts (the re-export of the moved handle types), packages/connectors/connector-mcp/src/mcp-provider.ts (read: the `providerConfig.transport.kind` vocabulary the mcp-http exception keys on), packages/qa/downstream-contract/src/additional-domains.fixtures.ts with its README (the frozen fixture the narrowing breaks), .changeset/28137-connector-grant-bearing-auth.md, and — the narrowing-face floor — every other path of the diff outside the prose faces (the five regenerated spec surfaces, variant-docs.json, the four test files, the pin test), all read.

Inputs: card #28137 body and its four comments (triage 6524666067, claim 6524922758, claim correction 6525266851 with the seat's ruling A and the narrowing re-declaration, os-dev-report 6528499617); PR #28213 body, 27-file list and the diff against `main` (+1301/-306); the check-runs on `c9b16a83` (read 2026-10-30T17:37Z): 50 runs over 50 names, all `completed`, 41 `success`, 9 `skipped`, 0 `failure`; among the successes Auto Label, Build & E2E UI, Build Core, Build Docs, Build UI Deps, Check Changeset, Check Documentation Links, Check PR Size, Dogfood Regression Gate, Flag docs affected by code changes, Governed Surface Queue Guard, Lint & Repo Gates, Lint · CI, release & engine gates, Lint · ESLint, Lint · PM dispatch-gates, Lint · docs & code guards, Lint · repo & tooling gates, Lint · scoped · query-options erasure, Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus, Lint · scoped · tooling self-tests, Live E2E UI, PR-body guards (claim · duplicate · Part-of · single-writer path), Plan Test Core shards, Spec property liveness, Test Core, Test UI, Type Check UI, Type Check · consumer gates, Type Check · debt ledger, Type Check · source gates, Type Check · workspace, TypeScript Type Check, filter, Test Core 1/8-8/8. Author `user.login` is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so no login note is owed. The reviewer is not the drafter (`session_01L9qibvmENgz1tZkajp5SuJ`). Head history: the report's head `4d12a278` was read in full and went red on `check-adr-symbol-anchors` (ADR-0143 lines 88 and 237 anchored the deleted `ConnectorOAuth2Schema`); `2ee1b723` re-anchored the ADR and `check-governed-merges` put `docs/adr/**` at Tier H; the seat ruled the ADR restored byte-for-byte with the token kept as a string literal in the prescription, which is the head reviewed here (delta read: `4d12a278..c9b16a83` is two commits whose net diff is two lines of `connector-auth.zod.ts`, the `CONNECTOR_AUTH_CONFIG_OAUTH2_RETIRED` prescription now opening with the retired schema's name; `docs/adr/**` has no diff against `main`).

### ① Derived judgments

- D2.1 `oauth2` holds against ADR-0143 D2 item 1 key for key: `grant` closed to the two RFC 6749 grants (`ConnectorOAuth2GrantSchema`); one `strictObject` per grant; `authorizationUrl` only on `authorization_code` (refused by name on `client_credentials`); `tokenUrl`, `scopes`, `resource` (the ADR's "optional resource / audience indicator", with `audience` as a strict-shape alias); `clientId` a plain string; the client secret only as `credentialRef`, optional on `authorization_code` (a public client) and required together with `clientId` on `client_credentials` (`dependentRequired`, projectable, so the JSON Schema carries both rules). No PKCE key, and `pkce` is refused with the D2.1 "no switch" sentence. The endpoint and client requirement rides on `DeclarativeConnectorEntrySchema` because it needs the provider: refused at `auth.tokenUrl` / `auth.clientId` / `auth.authorizationUrl` unless `provider: 'mcp'` with `providerConfig.transport.kind === 'http'`. That is the spelling `connector-mcp`'s `mcp-provider.ts` validates (`transport.kind` must be `'stdio'` or `'http'`), so the exception fires for exactly the transport that runs the MCP authorization flow, and a stdio mcp instance meets the ordinary refusals (pinned).
- D2.2 `app-credential` holds: `vendor` closed to `feishu | dingtalk | wecom`, `appId` non-secret with the vendors' own spellings (`appKey`, `corpId`, `clientId`) as aliases, `credentialRef` required; `appSecret` / `corpSecret` / `secret` and the token keys refused by name. D2.3: no `signed` member; the closed-union test pins that `signed` is refused at `type`.
- D3 at the publish door: every secret or token key an author could reach for on either kind is refused by name with the `credentialRef` prescription (`unrecognized_keys @ auth`), the ADR Acceptance's "inline secret on any variant refused at publish with a located error"; the keys that remain (`clientId`, `appId`, endpoints, `scopes`, `resource`) carry no secret.
- D7: `ConnectorOAuth2Schema` leaves `ConnectorAuthConfigSchema`; the union's `error` map raises the prescription only for `input.type === 'oauth2'` (the `ViewDataSchema` `provider: 'api'` precedent) and every other unknown discriminator keeps zod's own report (CONTROL pinned). The ADR-0087 D3 semantic entry `connector-auth-config-oauth2-retired` names surface, replacement, reason and acceptance criteria, with its `STEP18_RATIONALE` fragment; no D2 conversion is the right disposition, since the replacement lives on another surface and needs a secret moved out of the source. `ResolvedConnectorAuth` is unchanged (four static kinds), so `ConnectorProviderContext.auth` and every provider factory are untouched.
- D4: the four handle types move into `packages/spec/src/integration/connector-provider.ts` structurally identical to the `@objectstack/types` originals (same members, same doc contracts, the `503` refusal semantics kept), and `@objectstack/types` re-exports them under the same names, so `IConnectorCredentialSource.borrow` and its drivers keep their spelling; `@objectstack/types` already depends on `@objectstack/spec` (`workspace:*`). `credentialHandle?` on `ConnectorProviderContext` is optional and set by no host today — typed here, served by S1.
- First consumers under seat ruling A: the reconcile's grant-bearing branch sits before the `[#27237]` credential resolution and before `resolveInstanceAuth`, so a grant-bearing entry is held degraded with a reason naming its kind and is never materialized; `resolveInstanceAuth`'s parameter is narrowed with `Exclude<…, GrantBearingInstanceAuth>`, so the type system refuses a future path that hands it one. `connector-credential-source.ts` refuses a datasource borrow of such an instance in `lendRefusal` (`422`) before any handle is minted. Both stand-ins are enumerated for S1 in the PR body.
- The other union consumers (`connector-mcp`, `connector-openapi`, `connector-rest`, `driver-odata`) read `ResolvedConnectorAuth` / `BorrowedConnectorAuth`, not `ConnectorInstanceAuth`, so the widening cannot reach them; no ui/ reader of the instance auth kinds exists.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/spec` **minor** with **BREAKING**, `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` / `Metadata-protocol: narrowed`: the widening (two `ConnectorInstanceAuthSchema` members, six exports, `credentialHandle`) beside the narrowing (`integration/Connector:authentication` no longer accepts `type: 'oauth2'`). The level follows the launch-window convention that ships an accept-set narrowing as `minor` with a registered ADR-0087 entry (#28150, #27951 and the other `**BREAKING** … (narrowing)` entries on `main`); `check-changeset-no-major` admits `narrowed` beside `(narrowing)`, and the `authorable-surface/integration.json` baseline moves with the declaration. The `downstream-contract` fixture edit is the intended-break form its README asks for, documented in the changeset and the ADR-0087 entry (the README's "bump to a new major" wording predates the convention the gate now enforces — not this PR's to fix).
- `@objectstack/types` **patch**: a relocation re-exported under the same names, structurally unchanged; no accept set moves (the #28070 / #28151 precedent for an additive or relocated export).
- `@objectstack/service-automation` **patch**: a fail-closed refusal for a kind that could not be authored before this PR; the four static kinds' served behaviour does not move (CONTROL cases kept in both test files).
- The three carriers agree: PR body, claim correction 6525266851 and the changeset all say `yes (narrowing)` / `narrowed`.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Served at publish: `DeclarativeConnectorEntrySchema` is parsed by both authoring doors, so the new refusals land wherever an entry is authored; `connector-auth-grant-kinds.test.ts` pins each by `code @ path` with a CONTROL accept per member and for the mcp-http omission.
- Served at runtime, until S1: a grant-bearing instance degrades through the existing `failDegradedConnectorInstance` (so the connectors listing and the drift check see it as any other degraded instance), and a datasource borrow answers `422 VALIDATION_ERROR` naming the kind; nothing dispatches to an upstream unauthenticated.
- Governed: `docs/adr/**` is untouched on this head; ADR-0143's two `ConnectorOAuth2Schema` anchors resolve through the string-literal token in the prescription constant (line 51 of `connector-auth.zod.ts` carries the token in a string literal, which `symbol-anchors.mjs` resolves, while every other mention is comment prose it strips). `skills/**` untouched: the `integration-recipes.md` "Not yet" OAuth bullet stays correct until S1 serves the kind (the PR's `Skills-docs:` line, the dev's out-of-scope finding c).
- Tier: whole-PR diff +1301/-306 over 27 files, no `docs/adr/**`, `skills/**` or other governed row on this head ⇒ Tier S; the Tier H on `2ee1b723` was the ADR edit alone.
- Author `objectstack-fleet[bot]` ⇒ no login note. Dependency: S1 (#26702) replaces the stand-in lines the PR body enumerates; the skill bullet and `evals/integrations-declared.json` ride with S1.

### ④ Design judgment

- Schema against the ruling: each D2.1 / D2.2 key maps to a sentence of ADR-0143 D2 (① above); nothing the ADR forbids is authorable (a secret, a token, a PKCE switch, `signed`), nothing it requires is missing (closed enums, located refusals, the mcp-http omission, a pre-registered mcp client accepted). The one D2.1 topic the shape does not carry — how a pre-registered client authenticates at the token endpoint — the ADR leaves to the runtime, and triage 6524666067 ruled it the spec author's weighing that "does not get decided in the PR"; leaving it out of the shape is the conservative reading, and S1 adds a key under a decision card only if it needs one. Holds.
- First consumer: the only consumers today are the two stand-ins in `service-automation`, both fail-closed; the D4 types are consumed unchanged by the datasource borrow path. Holds.
- The narrowing against the published spec on `main`: the retired value had no first-party author (the frozen qa fixture was the single hit) and no runtime ever read its secret, so the narrowing takes nothing a consumer could use and makes the spec's own refusal real (no inline secret at rest); the prescription names the replacement surface and the D3 entry carries the judgement an upgrader owes. Holds.
- Risk read: `dependentRequired({ credentialRef: ['clientId'], clientId: ['credentialRef'] })` on `client_credentials` also lets an mcp-http instance omit both (dynamic registration), consistent with D2.1 and pinned; `resource` is `z.string().url()`, matching RFC 8707's absolute-URI form. A grant-bearing entry can degrade only after the entry parsed, so an operator sees the named reason, never a silent skip.

Should-fix, none blocking: (S1) `lint-flow-credential-literals.ts` steer strings and `rule-explanations.ts` still name only the static kinds — right until S1 serves a grant, then they widen with the skill bullet.

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么：** 连接器实例的 `auth` 新增两种需要换取令牌的类型：`oauth2`（授权码 / 客户端凭证）和 `app-credential`（飞书、钉钉、企业微信）。密钥只能写引用。旧的运行时 `oauth2` 写法 `authentication: { type: 'oauth2' }` 被移除，并给出改写提示（ADR-0087 条目）。
- **为什么改：** 以前对接要 OAuth 的系统在开源版里无处声明；旧写法把密钥和刷新令牌明文写进配置，也从来没人执行。ADR-0143 把这类认证纳入开源层，这是第一步 S0，只定形状。
- **风险与回滚：** 写了旧 `oauth2` 的连接器会被拒绝，并附迁移提示。新类型的实例在服务端（S1，#26702）真正支持前，一律标为“降级、不调用上游”，数据源借用返回 422，不会出现未认证调用。回滚即 revert。
- **先看：** `packages/spec/src/shared/connector-auth.zod.ts`，以及 `packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts` 新加的降级分支。
- **两分钟验证：** `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec exec vitest run src/integration/connector-auth-grant-kinds.test.ts src/shared/connector-auth.test.ts`。
- **需要你做的：** 无。不属于受管面，契约复审 PASS（评论 6529303069），由席位落地。
- **席位意见：** ACCEPT，可落地。
